title: Sell Mineral Rights in Camp Three, MT
primaryKeyword: sell mineral rights camp three mt
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Camp Three, MT
metaDescription: Camp Three sits in Musselshell County near the Roundup coalfield and the old Cat Creek oil field. A former engineer explains what that layered history means.
heroLead: Camp Three's name itself is a leftover from the Roundup coalfield's mining-camp days, and that layered coal-and-oil history is exactly what I check before valuing minerals here.
intro: Musselshell County built its early economy on coal, with mining camps numbered and named across the Roundup field in the early 1900s, Camp Three among them. What's less well known outside the industry is that this same general area of central Montana is also home to the Cat Creek oil field, discovered around 1920, one of the state's oldest producing conventional oil fields, sitting mostly in the Musselshell-Petroleum-Garfield county area.

sections.heading: Coal First, Then One of Montana's Original Oil Fields
paragraphs: If your family's mineral interest near Camp Three traces to the coal-mining era, check whether the original deed separated coal from oil, gas, and other minerals, since that split is common in this part of the state. Separately, Cat Creek's century of production means some tracts in the broader area carry real, if mature and slow-declining, conventional oil history rather than being purely speculative.

sections.heading: A Genuinely Old Field, Genuinely Slow Decline
paragraphs: Cat Creek has been producing, in some form, for roughly a century, and wells this old behave very differently than a Bakken horizontal. Royalty checks tied to this trend tend to be small and steady rather than large and front-loaded, which is a fair, honest description rather than a knock on the interest's value.

sections.heading: Evaluating a Camp Three-Area Tract
paragraphs: I'd check whether your deed splits coal from oil and gas, pull any current or historical division order tied to Cat Creek-area production, and confirm your net revenue interest against the recorded chain of title. Given the field's age, remaining reserve life and payment consistency matter more here than speculation about new drilling.

faqs.question: What is the Cat Creek oil field and is my Camp Three interest connected to it?
faqs.answer: Cat Creek is one of Montana's oldest conventional oil fields, discovered around 1920 in the broader Musselshell County area. Whether your specific tract is connected depends on its exact location, which a title search will confirm.

faqs.question: Does my deed near Camp Three include coal rights?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Given the Roundup coalfield's mining history in this area, many older deeds separate coal from oil, gas, and other minerals. Check the original severance language at the Musselshell County Clerk and Recorder in Roundup.

faqs.question: Why is my royalty check from an old well so small?
faqs.answer: Century-old conventional fields like Cat Creek decline slowly and produce modest, steady checks rather than the larger front-loaded payments typical of a new shale well. Small and steady is normal behavior for a field this mature.
